clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: How to describe what you do not know: random variables and distributions, conditioning and Bayes' rule, why averages settle and errors look Gaussian, and the matrix tools (covariance, Cholesky, SVD) every inversion uses.

clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: Turning data into a model when the data are not enough: least squares and its limits, Bayesian linear inversion and the MAP, regularisation as a prior, loss functions and optimisers, choosing a prior, and Gaussian-process priors on whole fields.

clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: Where errors come from and how to weight data: measurement noise (C_d) versus model error (C_p), and how the noise in GNSS, InSAR and tsunami records becomes a data covariance.

clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: Computing a posterior that has no formula: Metropolis, gradients and JAX, HMC and NUTS, convergence diagnostics and Monte Carlo error, tempering and SMC, variational inference, and gradients through physics.

clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: Inversion through time and with ensembles: the Kalman filter, ensemble Kalman methods (EnKF, EKI, EnKI), measuring nonlinearity, the extended Kalman filter, and localization for small ensembles.

clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: Choosing the knobs and comparing models: entropy and KL divergence, criteria for hyperparameters (L-curve, GCV, ABIC, AIC, BIC), hierarchical Bayes and data weights, and what objectivity can and cannot mean.

clusters.subject: Inverse problems and Bayesian inversion
clusters.summary: Using and checking the answer: derived quantities, intervals, joint statements, predictive checks, simulation-based calibration, model comparison by prediction, and one inversion with every choice side by side.
